title: dm_query_json response
description: What dm_query_json returns for each query. A failure is a dm_status with a message on dm_last_error rather than an error object here: DM_ERR_INVALID_ARG for a malformed request or unknown query, DM_ERR_NOT_FOUND for a path that is not in the tree. An empty result is DM_OK with an empty array, since a type with no subtypes is an answer.

ancestorsOfResponse.description: Added at ABI 0.14. The whole inheritance chain in one call instead of one objectTree round trip per level.

ancestors.description: Nearest first, self excluded, each rendered as a depth-0 node (children empty, childCount still says how many exist). Empty for a type with no parent - /datum, /list, /client, /savefile - and for the root.

referencesResponse.description: Added at ABI 0.14. Every use of a symbol across the project, found by the binder's own resolution - the same one the diagnostics use - so the index and the squiggles cannot disagree. Locals and parameters are not index symbols. A path that names no symbol is DM_OK with an empty list, not DM_ERR_NOT_FOUND.

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the list short. Reported rather than inferred, as for subtypesOf.

overriddenProcResponse.description: Added at ABI 0.31. What THIS type's definition of a proc overrides - the inverse of the references query's "override" kind. A fresh declaration overriding nothing is an answer (overrides: false, owner ""), not an error; it is what dm.exe's own no_parent warning reports on. DM_ERR_NOT_FOUND only when the path is not in the tree or name is empty.

overrides.description: Draw a "go to overridden" affordance from this flag rather than from whether the call succeeded.

owner.description: The type whose definition is overridden, or "" when overrides is false. The builtin case is the type's OWN: a project's /mob/Login() overrides /mob's builtin, so owner is /mob.

builtin.description: True when the overridden definition is BYOND's. Nothing declares a builtin, so there is nothing to open - which is why this is separate from owner.

file.description: The file holding the use, spelled as the workspace spells it.

kind.description: "override" hits are proc declarations overriding the target - the incoming half of a type hierarchy.

inside.description: The enclosing symbol - "/mob/hurt()" for a proc body, a type path for a type-level initialiser. Group hits by it and you have a call hierarchy.

startChar.description: In the request's "encoding", utf16 by default. The four position keys are omitted only when the file's text could not be read.

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the list short. Reported rather than inferred from the count, because a list exactly as long as the limit looks identical to one that was cut.

types.description: Flat and in tree order. The type asked about is not included.

declared.description: False for a node that exists only because something deeper was declared: /obj/item/sword alone brings /obj/item into being.

parentType.description: Where the type INHERITS from, which is not always its path parent - /mob is a child of the root by path and inherits from /atom/movable. Null at the root.

childCount.description: How many children exist, which is not the length of "children" when depth cut the response short. This is what lets a panel draw an expander without a second call.

detail.description: The declaration as written: a signature for a proc, the declared type for a var.

kind.description: dm_symbol_kind, the same values dm_document_symbols uses.

inherited.description: True when the member is declared on an ancestor rather than on the type asked about.

owner.description: The type the member is declared on.

file.description: Empty for a builtin, since nothing in the project declares it.
